picks.matchup: North Carolina Tar Heels @ TCU Horned Frogs
picks.title: North Carolina Tar Heels +8.5
picks.title_full: North Carolina Tar Heels +8.5, full game, -110
picks.rationale: The model has TCU by 4.9 at a neutral site in Dublin against a market laying 8.5, and the research explains that gap rather than closing it. North Carolina defensive coordinator Steve Belichick has been on indefinite medical leave since August 6 and is not expected to travel, leaving Bill Belichick to call the defense alongside line coach Bob Diaco in the season opener. TCU returns 11 starters while North Carolina turned its roster over again in year two, and in August returning production is the honest tiebreaker that the ratings do not carry. That is why the number sits three and a half points past the model, and why I am logging this instead of betting it. What would make me wrong is Bill Belichick calling a sharper game than his son would have and Bobby Petrino's offense arriving fully formed in week 0.

sources.quote: Belichick, the son of UNC head coach Bill Belichick, has been away from the program on an indefinite medical leave since August 6.

picks.matchup: San Jose State Spartans @ USC Trojans
picks.title: San Jose State Spartans +38.5
picks.title_full: San Jose State Spartans +38.5, full game, -104
picks.rationale: The model has USC by 35.4 and the market is laying 38.5, but those three points came from somewhere: the game opened at 35.5 with a total of 57.5 and has moved to 38.5 and 61.5, everything pushing the same direction. Taking the Spartans means fading that move on nothing but a ratings number that is simply the opening line restated. San Jose State went 3-9 last season and USC opens ranked 14th with Jayden Maiava back after leading the Big Ten in passing yards, so there is no researched reason to think the move is wrong. A number that walks three points toward the favourite in a game nobody has to bet is not one I want the other side of empty handed. What would make me wrong is Lincoln Riley clearing the bench up 40 in the third quarter, which is exactly how these numbers get covered backwards.

picks.title: NC State Wolfpack +4.5
picks.rationale: Virginia loses its projected No. 1 receiver, Rico Flores, to a hamstring, and Beau Pribula makes his first start for the Cavaliers after going 4 touchdowns against 8 interceptions versus SEC defenses at Missouri in 2025, while NC State brings back CJ Bailey and his 22 career FBS starts. Virginia is being priced off an 11-3 season that reached the ACC championship game, which is the kind of outlier year the market carries forward too far. The headline injury number is misleading and I am not leaning on it: the ACC report listed 16 Cavaliers out, but Flores is the only starter or second-teamer among them. This stays a shadow pick because the market got here first, moving from 5.5 to 4.5 and dropping the total from 53.5 to 51.5, and the blended model saw no gap in this game at all, so there is a real argument and no price left to pay for it. What makes me wrong is Pribula playing clean behind a line that returns intact and Virginia running for 200 on a Wolfpack front that has to prove it.

picks.matchup: Jacksonville State Gamecocks @ North Dakota State Bison
picks.title: Over 46.5
picks.rationale: The model wants this Over by 9.5 points while the market has moved the other way, from 47.5 down to 46.5, and a market moving against a large model edge is usually the market telling you the rating is stale. North Dakota State is playing its first game as an FBS program with a new quarterback in Nathan Hayes and several new starters on the offensive line, details I took from previews I could not open to quote directly, and the Bison profile has always been a run-first clock-eating one that does not produce the totals these blended ratings project. Jacksonville State is also breaking in a new quarterback. The Fargodome takes weather off the table as an argument for the Under, which is the only thing holding this at 6.0 instead of lower. What would make me wrong is both defenses being as unready as both offenses and this turning into the track meet the ratings expect.

picks.matchup: Sacramento State Hornets @ Eastern Michigan Eagles
picks.title: Sacramento State Hornets +9.5
picks.rationale: The model makes Eastern Michigan 5.4 against a market laying 9.5, but Sacramento State carries the least trustworthy rating on this board: SP+ has the Hornets at minus 23.4 and FPI at minus 10.4, a 13 point disagreement that means neither system knows what this team is. Sacramento State plays its first FBS game with Alonzo Carter debuting as head coach, Carson Conklin taking the snaps after a year at Fresno State, and a roster the school itself describes as 73 newcomers against six returning starters. Eastern Michigan brings back Noah Kim, who threw for 2,817 yards last season. The one live argument for the Hornets is that Eastern Michigan allowed the worst rushing average in the country in 2025, a claim I found only in a College Football News preview I could not open to quote, so I am not weighting it. What would make me wrong is that run defense being exactly as bad as advertised against a Sacramento State roster built to run at it.

picks.title: Hawaii Rainbow Warriors +3.5
picks.rationale: Stanford opens under a first-year head coach in Tavita Pritchard with Davis Warren having just won the quarterback job in camp, while Hawaii returns Micah Alejado, who finished 2025 eighth nationally in passing yards per game at 282.4 and second in FBS in completions per game, and a head coach in year five. Hawaii won this same season opener against Stanford 23-20 a year ago. The blended model has Stanford by 2.6 and the market is laying 3.5, so the ratings contribute almost nothing here and the whole case is continuity against a new staff. That case is thinner than it first looks, because Hawaii has to replace 17 starters of its own and returns only eight, which is why this is logged at 7.2 rather than played. What makes me wrong is Warren being an immediate upgrade at Stanford and the Cardinal front controlling a Hawaii offensive line that lost most of its starters.

picks.matchup: New Mexico State Aggies @ Florida State Seminoles
picks.title: New Mexico State Aggies +32.5
picks.title_full: New Mexico State Aggies +32.5, full game, -115
picks.rationale: The model has Florida State by 29.5 against a market laying 32.5, and here too the number moved away from the model rather than toward it, opening around 30.5 and settling at 32.5. New Mexico State went through camp without settling its quarterback, with Adam Damante, Furman transfer Trey Hedden and JUCO arrival Kalani McLeod all in the mix, which is the worst way to walk into Doak Campbell Stadium. Florida State has missed a bowl in consecutive seasons and Mike Norvell needs a fast start, so the incentive to keep scoring into the fourth quarter is there rather than absent. Three points of model disagreement does not buy a 32.5 point underdog whose offense does not know who is taking the snap. What would make me wrong is Ashton Daniels starting slowly in his own first game for Florida State and the score sitting in the twenties late.

picks.title: Over 56.5
picks.rationale: This is the largest gap on the board, the model at 66.8 against a market total of 56.5, and I am logging it as a shadow pick because every piece of research runs the other way. Both offenses are new: Charles Huff has taken over at Memphis with the quarterback job still open between Marcus Stokes and Air Noland, and Dan Mullen has declined to name a starter, saying both Jackson Arnold and Alex Orji will play for UNLV. The model's 66.8 is assembled from last season's offensive ratings for two units that no longer exist, and a rotating quarterback is a drag on rhythm rather than a shootout ingredient. Ten points of disagreement in week 0 with new staffs on both sidelines is far more likely a stale rating than a soft number, and this is the cleanest test the ledger will get of whether the totals model can be trusted in August. What would make me wrong is the roof at Allegiant taking weather out of it while two defenses break in as many new starters as the offenses do.
